liabilityCap.title: 1. Liability cap
liabilityCap.requireLabel: Require a cap on your financial liability
liabilityCap.requireHelp: Protects you from unlimited financial claims if a dispute happens.
liabilityCap.multipleLabel: Maximum cap (multiple of contract fees, 0.5 to 10)
liabilityCap.multipleHelp: Limits your total liability to this multiple of the fees you receive.

paymentTerms.title: 2. Payment terms
paymentTerms.maxDaysLabel: Maximum days to get paid (1 to 120)
paymentTerms.maxDaysHelp: Caps how long a client can wait after invoicing before payment is overdue.

ipOwnership.title: 3. IP ownership
ipOwnership.selectLabel: When work ownership transfers to the client
ipOwnership.selectHelp: Prevents losing ownership rights before your invoice is paid in full.

termination.title: 4. Termination
termination.noticeHelp: Gives you advance notice before a client can end active work.
termination.payWorkDoneLabel: Require payment for work already done
termination.payWorkDoneHelp: Ensures completed milestones or hours are paid even if cancelled early.

scopeChanges.title: 5. Scope changes
scopeChanges.writtenOrderHelp: Stops unpaid extra work by requiring written approval before scope expands.

findingsPane.defaultVsLine: Contract terms differ from standard rules.
findingsPane.defaultRecommendation: Ask the client to clarify or amend this term.

PAY-1.title: Payment deadline exceeds playbook limit
PAY-1.vsLine: Your rule: {playbook_max_days} days vs Contract: {days_to_pay} days
PAY-1.reason: Payment timeline is longer than your preferred limit, increasing cash flow risk.
PAY-1.recommendation: Ask for payment within {playbook_max_days} days of invoice.
PAY-1.financialConsequence: Payment of {amount} {currency} could arrive {days_to_pay} days after {event}.

PAY-2.title: Payment conditional on client acceptance or withholding permitted
PAY-2.vsLine: Contract allows delayed payment triggers or client withholding.
PAY-2.reason: Client can delay payment pending subjective acceptance or withhold fees unilaterally.
PAY-2.recommendation: Ask for payment tied to delivery or invoice receipt, and remove unilateral withholding.

PAY-3.title: Payment timeline missing or unspecified
PAY-3.vsLine: Contract does not clearly define days to pay.
PAY-3.reason: Without an explicit payment deadline, payment timing is legally uncertain.
PAY-3.recommendation: Ask for a clear payment deadline (e.g., net 15 or net 30 calendar days).
PAY-3.uncertainty: Contract omits or obscures standard payment timeline.

LIAB-1.title: Liability cap missing, unlimited, or exceeds limit
LIAB-1.vsLine: Your rule requires capped liability vs Contract terms.
LIAB-1.reason: Unlimited or un-capped liability puts all your business and personal assets at risk.
LIAB-1.recommendation: Ask for a liability cap equal to or less than total fees paid under this agreement.

IP-1.title: Intellectual property transfers before full payment
IP-1.reason: Transferring IP ownership before payment is received leaves you without leverage if the client defaults.
IP-1.recommendation: Ask for IP ownership to transfer only upon receipt of full payment.

TERM-1.title: Client convenience termination notice period too short
TERM-1.vsLine: Your rule: {min_notice_days} days notice vs Contract: {notice_days} days
TERM-1.reason: The client can terminate abruptly with insufficient notice, leaving unbillable pipeline gaps.
TERM-1.recommendation: Ask for at least {min_notice_days} days written notice before convenience termination.

TERM-2.title: No guaranteed payment for work completed upon termination
TERM-2.vsLine: Your rule: payment for all work done vs Contract: {payment_for_work_done}
TERM-2.reason: Contract does not guarantee fair pro-rata payment for time and deliverables completed before termination.
TERM-2.recommendation: Ask for clause confirming full pro-rata compensation for all work completed up to termination date.

SCOPE-1.title: Extra work without change order or fee
SCOPE-1.vsLine: Your rule requires written change orders before performing extra work.
SCOPE-1.reason: Contract allows client to request extra tasks without written change orders or additional fees.
SCOPE-1.recommendation: Ask for a requirement that all scope additions be agreed in a written signed change order with additional compensation.

LAW-1.title: Foreign governing law and jurisdiction
LAW-1.reason: Contract is governed by foreign law or foreign arbitration, creating heavy cost and legal hurdles if a dispute arises.
LAW-1.recommendation: Ask for governing law of Bangladesh, or at least dispute resolution within Bangladesh.
LAW-1.uncertainty: Enforcing foreign judgments or arbitrating abroad is cost-prohibitive for local developers.

IND-1.title: Broad one-sided contractor indemnity
IND-1.vsLine: Contract imposes broad indemnification on contractor.
IND-1.reason: You are required to hold the client harmless against broad claims, potentially covering third-party losses.
IND-1.recommendation: Ask to limit indemnity to direct damages caused by your gross negligence or breach, or make indemnity mutual.

DEF-1.title: Defined losses include indirect or consequential damages
DEF-1.reason: The contract defines recoverable losses to include indirect or consequential damages.
DEF-1.recommendation: Ask to expressly exclude indirect, incidental, and consequential damages.
